feedback: If a learner gives 180 minutes for 3 h 25 min, ask where the 25 minutes went; have them add the remainder back: 180 + 25 = 205. A bar model separating the whole units (3 × 60 = 180) from the remainder (25) can make the two-part split visible when the leftover is dropped.
If a learner reads 150 seconds as '1.5 minutes', group the seconds into sixties: two complete sixties and 30 left, so 2 minutes 30 seconds — 150 ÷ 60 = 2 remainder 30.
If a learner answers '2 minutes' for 150 seconds, point to the 30 seconds still unaccounted for and ask what happens to them.
If a learner uses ×100 for hours→minutes, contrast their answer with grouping into sixties so the 60-grouping is visibly correct.
activities.intendedInsight: Converting units of time is multiply (by the fixed rate) then combine the remainder — not counting up — and for seconds, minutes and hours the grouping is 60, not 100.
learnerActions: Take a mixed quantity such as 3 hours 25 minutes and convert it: multiply the whole units by the rate (3 × 60 = 180 minutes), then add the remaining 25 to get 205 minutes.
State out loud whether you counted up or multiplied, and why multiplying is faster.
Work a reverse conversion: take 150 seconds, group it into sixties — two full groups of 60 make 2 minutes, with 30 seconds left over, giving '2 minutes 30 seconds'.
Test the tempting '100 to a minute' idea against grouping real seconds into sixties, and describe what goes wrong.
activities.title: Multiply-then-combine with a conversion machine

feedback: For '1.5 minutes', re-ground on 60: 1.5 of 60 would be 90 seconds, not 150; 150 seconds is 2 minutes 30 seconds.
For '2 minutes', ask about the leftover 30 seconds.
For 8 weeks 3 days, confirm 8 × 7 = 56 then add the 3 loose days for 59.
activities.intendedInsight: Secure conversions rest on known multiplication facts and on keeping the remainder; the common wrong answers to the 150-seconds item — '1.5 minutes' and '2 minutes' — correspond to base-10 thinking and to dropping the remainder.
learnerActions: Fill in conversions such as '3 h 25 min = ___ min' and show the multiply-then-add working.
Match a seconds amount (e.g. 150 s) to its minutes-and-seconds form.
Choose the correct reading of 150 seconds and explain why '1.5 minutes' (base-10 thinking) and '2 minutes' (dropped remainder) are both wrong.
Convert 8 weeks 3 days to days using 8 × 7 = 56, then + 3 = 59 days.
activities.title: Known-facts conversion with a base-10 trap item

feedback: If a learner converts months to days as ×28 or calls a month exactly 4 weeks, use the calendar to show months of 28, 30 and 31 days and distinguish the approximate month fact from the exact week-to-day fact.
activities.intendedInsight: Some time units convert by exact fixed rates (7 days per week, 60 seconds per minute, 12 months per year) while month LENGTHS are irregular, so 'a month ≈ 4 weeks' cannot be used as an exact conversion to days.
learnerActions: Use a real calendar to count the days in several different months, including February, and record what you find: months have 28, 29 (February in a leap year), 30 or 31 days.
State why 'about 4 weeks in a month' is an approximation, not an exact conversion.
Contrast the exact fact (1 week = 7 days) with the approximate month fact, and explain how you would convert months to days versus weeks to days.
activities.title: Irregular units: months, weeks and the calendar

feedback: Ask the learner to justify their chosen rate; if they add rather than multiply, prompt them to build the ×rate from a known fact.
Probe the remainder: 'Did you keep the leftover part, and where did it go in your answer?'
activities.intendedInsight: Conversions apply in context; choosing the right rate and correctly expressing mixed/remainder answers is part of solving the problem.
learnerActions: Read or hear a word problem (e.g. 'A film lasts 150 seconds — how long is that in minutes and seconds?') and solve it, saying each step aloud.
Explain for each problem which rate you used (×60, ×7, ×12) and how you handled any remainder or second unit.
activities.title: Pose-and-solve conversion word problems
